content.text:
I submitted **index 59** (Bi 0.12, Cu 0.27, V 0.61) as the best composition. At 6.01 µA, it had the highest photocurrent of the three I could measure. I don't know how it compares with the best composition in the library.

I used the whole merit budget of 3 measurements:

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent | Why I chose it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 293 | 0.40 / 0.19 / 0.41 | 1.24 µA | Closest to BiVO₄ (1:1 Bi:V, a known photoanode) with the least Cu |
| 1 | 0.15 / 0.26 / 0.59 | 4.12 µA | Middle of the V-rich, Cu-containing region, where the library has the most samples |
| 59 | 0.12 / 0.27 / 0.61 | 6.01 µA | A step further in the direction that had raised photocurrent |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose each time I moved to less Bi and more V, and slightly more Cu. The peak may lie further in that direction or somewhere untested, such as the Cu-rich corner. With three points I couldn't check.
- **Model suggestions not followed:** I skipped the Gaussian-process model's picks. Its first suggestion, index 150, sat near the weak Bi-rich result. I didn't take its second, index 68, either: I kept following the trend in the data and went to index 59.
- **XRD not used:** I didn't spend any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I can't say which crystal phases are behind the higher photocurrent.
